title: Rate limits: a refilling bucket, in-flight cap and shared limit
lede: Request-rate caps run on a continuously refilling bucket, with an in-flight cap for LLM calls; limits can be shared across the gateway cluster through Redis; MCP and A2A applications get their own app-wide RPM and max-concurrent caps (release notes). Units, numbers, the refusal the client sees and how the caps interact are the lab’s own model.

steps.title: A refilling bucket
steps.what: Request-rate caps run on a bucket that refills continuously, so a burst drains it and capacity returns gradually, not all at once as a fixed window would (lab model).
steps.why: Release notes: a continuously refilling bucket. The side-by-side with a fixed window is the lab’s own model. Spike protection is shown only as the bucket’s burst.

steps.title: In-flight cap for LLM calls
steps.what: LLM calls are also held to an in-flight cap. In the lab model slow calls hold slots, so the next call can be refused even when the request rate is low.

steps.title: App-wide caps for MCP and A2A
steps.what: MCP and A2A applications get their own app-wide requests-per-minute and max-concurrent caps (release notes).
steps.why: Lab model: that these are separate from a key’s caps, and that one agent can use up the app’s cap for the others.

steps.title: Shared across the cluster
steps.what: Limits can be shared across the gateway cluster through Redis (release notes). In the lab model, without sharing each node would allow the full limit, so a client could get several times it.

steps.title: A refusal
steps.what: In the lab model, when the bucket is empty, no slot is free or an app-wide cap is reached, the call is refused.
steps.why: UNVERIFIED: the client’s refusal shape. Open question, not shown here: whether a rate-limit refusal can trigger a model fallback.
